terms.grammar: adverb, before or after the word it stresses
evidence: Publ. E 13: Etiam capillus ūnus habet umbram suam.
terms.comment: Also with comparatives, “even more”: etiam dēterius quam soleō, even worse than usual (Cic. Fam. 5.14.1). “Not even” is nē … quidem.

terms.grammar: adverb: with superlatives, and “even” of something one may choose
evidence: Quint. 10.7.25: vel sōlī tamen dīcāmus potius quam omnīnō nōn dīcāmus
Cic. Att. 7.10.1: crēbrō ad mē scrībe vel quod in buccam vēnerit
terms.comment: “Even, if you like”: vel quod in buccam vēnerit, even whatever comes into your head; with a superlative, “the very”: vel maximus (Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: adverb, before the word it stresses

phrases.latin: Etiam capillus ūnus habet umbram suam.
phrases.english: Even a single hair has its own shadow.

phrases.latin: mox diēs vērus; sōl etiam effulsit
phrases.english: soon it was real daylight; the sun even shone out
Even when the wound has healed, the scar remains.
